name: FRRouting (FRR)
what_it_is: FRR is free software that implements and manages IPv4/IPv6 routing protocols on Linux and BSD systems. It runs as a suite of individual protocol daemons coordinated by a central routing engine (zebra) and exposes a CLI (vtysh), REST/YANG interfaces for configuration.
components: zebra (core routing engine and kernel interface)
measurement: BGP neighbor state and prefix counts (via show bgp summary)
OSPF adjacency state and LSA database
BFD session state and packet counters
PIM neighbor and multicast route table
Route table entries per VRF (via show ip route)
YANG-modeled operational state queryable via RESTCONF/NETCONF
configuration: Unified vtysh CLI with running-config and startup-config
YANG data models via northbound API (sysrepo/netopeer2 backends)
Route maps and prefix lists for policy
modes: Standalone daemon mode (each protocol runs as separate process)
Integrated vtysh CLI mode (single shell across all daemons)
Containerlab node mode (used as a network topology node)
constraints: Requires Linux kernel 5.4+ (or compatible BSD) for full feature support including MPLS and VRF
EIGRP and NHRP are marked alpha status and not production-ready
NETCONF/YANG northbound requires external sysrepo and netopeer2 services — not bundled
Does not implement a data-plane forwarder — relies on Linux kernel or external DPDK/P4 data planes
No built-in traffic generation or packet capture capability
Containerlab topology file required for multi-node lab orchestration — FRR alone cannot define topology
notable_absences: No built-in data plane (relies entirely on Linux kernel forwarding)
No traffic generator or packet injector
No GUI or web dashboard (only CLI and RESTCONF/NETCONF APIs)
No built-in fault injection or impairment features
No MPLS data-plane hardware offload (software forwarding only)
No docker-compose file in the repository (single-container image only)
NETCONF support requires external netopeer2 server, not included in the FRR image
